subject: MedSync streaming UX: post-call recap, model recs & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-09T16:12:00Z
Subject: MedSync streaming UX: quick recap + next steps

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed next step so everyone's aligned.

Key points I noted from the call:
- Primary goal: embed real-time summarization in the clinician mobile workflow with partial streaming so users can see progress as the model builds the summary.
- Pain: partial outputs are sometimes incoherent mid-sentence and stop sequences trigger early, which confuses clinicians.
- Latency target: 150ms p50 for single-turn generation; your current 300–400ms spikes are visible in the demo.
- Success criteria: 95% of streamed updates are sentence-coherent; stop-sequence reliability >99% for the clinical template.

Proposed next step: a 3-day focused eval run we run from Redwood's Dedicated staging environment to measure partial-output coherence, stop-sequence accuracy, and token-level latency. Deliverables: benchmark CSV, short report with model recommendations, and a minimal prompt-set that reproduces the issue.

I attached a starter prompt set and a sample runbook we plan to follow. If that's ok, we'll schedule the runs for Thursday and share results Friday morning.

Action items
- Alex: confirm scope + share the clinician template you want enforced for stop sequences (or paste in reply).
- Ben: I'll need a quick quote for the Dedicated-dev slot and estimated hours for the eval run.
- Alex/Lisa: any procurement gatekeepers we should loop in now?

Thanks — chloe

--
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments (3): medsync_promptset_v1.txt (text/plain), streaming_latency_bench_v2.csv (text/csv), medsync_eval_runbook.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@medsync.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MedSync streaming UX: quick recap + next steps

Thanks Chloe — that recap is perfect. A few clarifications: 

- Clinician template: I'll paste the exact JSON template below (used in prod). Stop sequences must align exactly to the "\n\n--END" marker. When the model emits that marker mid-stream that's a hard error for us.
- Priority: coherence > latency for now — clinicians prefer a slightly slower but readable partial update vs frequent nonsense.
- Procurement: Lisa is our procurement manager; she will own any PO.

On scope: yes to the 3-day focused eval. Two asks:
1) Please include both the lower-latency RW-7B-lowlat candidate and the higher-capacity RW-13B-stream candidate in the run so we can compare tradeoffs.
2) Add a short run that simulates congested network conditions (200ms added jitter) so we can see how the stop sequences behave under packet loss.

I'll attach the template in a follow-up if the email system strips JSON — copying small snippet below for quick reference.

On Thu, Feb 10, 2027 at 09:03, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.ai> wrote:
> Clinician stop marker: --END
> Example partial expected output: "Patient presents with chest pain. Impression: acute coronary syndrome ruled out based on troponin..."

Thanks — Alex

Alex Johnson
Head of Product, MedSync
alex.johnson@medsync.ai

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T14:26:00Z
Subject: Re: MedSync streaming UX: quick recap + next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the note and the stop marker. Plan and model choices below.

Planned eval matrix (3 days)
- Day 1: Baseline runs on your template with RW-13B-stream-8q (higher-capacity quantized) and RW-7B-lowlat (latency-optimized). Capture token-level timestamps to compute p50/p90 latency and first-token delay.
- Day 2: Stress tests with simulated network jitter (+200ms) and reduced batch sizing to mimic peak load. Focus on stop-sequence false-positive/false-negative rates.
- Day 3: Prompt-set iter + short prompt surgery (stop tokens and guard rails) to try to eliminate mid-sentence termination while observing latency changes.

Model recommendations (initial)
- RW-13B-stream-8q: Expected highest coherence, medium latency when quantized. Good for clinical templates where correctness is critical.
- RW-7B-lowlat: Lower token processing time and better p50/p90 latency, but historically more prone to hallucinated stops on edge prompt shapes.
- Fallback policy: if RW-13B p50 > 2x target under realistic token length, use RW-7B with server-side prefix caching and longer stop guard.

Deliverables we'll share Friday:
- streaming_latency_bench_v2.csv (latency by token + round-trip under each condition)
- medsync_promptset_v1.txt (prompt pairs that reproduce the issue)
- short recommendation note with suggested production config (batching, caching, stop token guard, quantization profile)

Attachments: I've uploaded the runbook and the prompt-set to the Drive link below. We'll kick off Thursday 08:00 PST and ping you at completion. If procurement signoff blocks access, loop Lisa now.

Links:
- Benchmark folder: https://drive.redwood.team/MedSync/benchmarks/streaming_latency_v2
- Eval runbook: doc:medsync-eval-promptset-v1

If that matches expectations I'll ask Ben to scope the Dedicated hours and send a small SOW. Marissa — can you confirm we have the dedicated-dev slot Thursday morning and how many GPU-hours we'd estimate for two models over 24 hours?

Best — chloe

--
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: MedSync eval run — quote & config ask

Ben / Marissa — quick internal note after Alex confirmed scope. Need a dual-model Dedicated-dev slot Thursday 08:00–20:00 PST. Rough asks:
- Target instance: 2x A10-equivalent (or 1x A100 if more cost-effective) for isolation.
- Estimate total GPU-hours: ~24 GPU-hours per model (run variety + stress tests) — please validate.
- Quote: propose a SOW line item for focused eval + one-day engineering support ($X hourly). I'll be the tech lead for the run.

Also: Marissa, can your team prep a short quality checklist for partial-output coherence so we can mark pass/fail per prompt? Suggested checks: complete-sentence score, stop-sequence accuracy, truncation frequency. We'll keep it intentionally lightweight.

I'll attach the prompt-set to the HubSpot deal once we have Ben's estimate so procurement can attach PO.

Thanks — chloe
